**Analyzing method counts**

I'm considering methods and receiver names within a functions package. I can focus on using an awk script to collect the function names and then count them using regular expressions. I need to handle method names as well and keep track of declarations. Using shell loops with awk seems efficient. Ultimately, I will aim to output the counts, parsing the declaration names accurately. It'll be interesting to see the top counts emerge!

args.command: for name in $(awk '/^func / {x=$2; sub(/\(.*/,"",x); sub(/\(.*/,"",x); print x} /^func \(/ {x=$3; sub(/\(.*/,"",x); print x}' $(find internal -name '*.go' -type f ! -name '*_test.go') | sort -u); do n=$(awk -v x="$name" '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ "(^|[^[:alnum:]_])" x "([^[:alnum:]_]|$)") c++} END{print c+0}' $(find . -name '*.go' -type f ! -name '*_test.go')); printf '%4d %s\n' "$n" "$name"; done | sort -rn | awk 'NR<=30 {print}'

**Analyzing function declarations**

I'm parsing some code and noticing that there's a generic method named 'New,' but it's not providing useful output. It seems like there are many declarations using the same name, which isn't ideal. I need to find out if `NewClient` is a key function since it has a high count of constructors. 

I should identify all package internal declarations and check the specific calls like `internal/httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` and `internal/markdown.NewService`. The question revolves around which function has the highest inbound-call count, and I need to refine my approach for accuracy.
**Refining function name extraction**

I'm working on using awk to correctly extract function names from Go declaration lines, but my current extraction method is flawed. The issue arises when `$2` represents method receivers, and `$3` captures the function name, which can lead to confusing outputs like `*Client)`. 

I need to adjust my script to count occurrences only when `$2` starts with `(`, and if not, I should use `$2`. I'll also make sure to exclude any generated or non-test Go files while outputting the top names.

args.command: for name in $(awk '/^func / {if ($2 ~ /^\(/) x=$3; else x=$2; sub(/\(.*/,"",x); print x}' $(find internal -name '*.go' -type f ! -name '*_test.go') | sort -u); do n=$(awk -v x="$name" '{line=$0; gsub(/[^[:alnum:]_]/," ",line); for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==x) c++} END{print c+0}' $(find . -name '*.go' -type f ! -name '*_test.go')); printf '%4d %s\n' "$n" "$name"; done | sort -rn | awk 'NR<=40 {print}'
